questionText: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can distinguish replacement state from patch instructions, choose PUT or PATCH for a concrete update, and protect either update from overwriting a newer version.
inScope: JSON Merge Patch and JSON Patch
outOfScope: A universal rule that omitted PUT fields become null
A claim that PATCH is always idempotent

claims.statement: PUT asks that the target resource's state be created or replaced with the state defined by the enclosed representation, and PUT is idempotent by method semantics.
HTTP defines PUT in terms of target-resource state and a representation; it does not define a universal mapping from omitted representation fields to null database columns.
PATCH applies the changes described by a typed patch document and is neither safe nor idempotent by its general method definition, although a particular patch can be idempotent.
JSON Merge Patch adds or replaces members named in an object, leaves unmentioned members unchanged, and gives null the special meaning of removing an existing member.
JSON Patch is an ordered array of operation objects and defines operations including add, remove, replace, move, copy, and test.
A server must apply the complete PATCH document atomically and must not apply any changes when the full patch cannot be applied successfully.
If-Match makes a state-changing request conditional on the current entity tag and can prevent an update from overwriting an unexpected newer representation.

examples.title: PUT and JSON Merge Patch for the same profile

validation.command: Parse the PUT and PATCH requests separately and check Content-Type, JSON bodies, and If-Match semantics
validation.expected: The PUT body represents target state; the PATCH body is valid JSON Merge Patch; both carry a valid conditional request field

visuals.title: Replacement state versus typed change instructions

notes: RFC 7396 is used for JSON Merge Patch and replaces the older RFC 7386 citation.
The lesson explicitly removes the common but false universal claim that every omitted PUT field becomes null.

review.notes: PUT, PATCH, both JSON patch formats, atomic application, and conditional-update claims were checked against their exact RFCs.
